thoughts.content: Confirmed symptom: frontend nginx is actively returning intermittent 500s (and earlier 502s) for /api/items right now — e.g. 21:02:17 500, 21:02:21 500, 21:02:23 500 — proxied to upstream http://10.96.255.102:8080/items (the api service). This matches the alert. Early 502 "Connection refused" at 21:01:03-21:01:07 suggests the api backend was still starting. Now investigating the api pods for the cause of intermittent 500s.

Root cause candidate found: a third pod shop-api-69f6fc5964-twjf9 carries label app=api (same as the legitimate api Deployment) and is crashing on every /items request with KeyError: 'DATABASE_URL' because its container is missing a DATABASE_URL env var. Since the api Service selects on app=api, this broken pod is likely being load-balanced into the same endpoint pool as the 2 healthy api-f64486c4c-* pods. Let me verify the Service endpoints and check the deployment spec for shop-api to confirm.

RCA Summary — HighErrorRate shop/frontend

Classification: CONFIRMED

What's happening right now
Frontend nginx pods are actively returning intermittent 500/502 on /api/items proxied to http://10.96.255.102:8080 (the api ClusterIP Service), e.g.:
``
21:02:17 "GET /api/items" 500
21:02:21 "GET /api/items" 500
21:02:23 "GET /api/items" 500
`
This confirms the alert symptom (5xx on /api/) is live, not just historical log noise.

Root cause chain
kubectl get endpoints api -n shop shows 3 backend endpoints behind the api Service: 10.244.1.148, 10.244.2.137 (the correct api Deployment, 2 replicas) and 10.244.2.140 — which belongs to a different, unrelated Deployment named shop-api (created ~8s after the correct api deployment, revision 1, 1 replica).
The api Service selects purely on label app=api. The shop-api Deployment's pod template carries labels app=api, app.kubernetes.io/name=shop-api — the shared app=api label causes it to be picked up as a valid endpoint of the api Service even though it's a separate deployment with separate (and broken) code.
That pod runs /code/app.py (not /code/api.py like the real api deployment) and every request throws:
   `
   KeyError: 'DATABASE_URL'
   File "/code/app.py", line 5, in settings
       return {"db": os.environ["DATABASE_URL"], ...}
   10.244.2.138 "GET /items HTTP/1.0" 500 -
   `
   The shop-api Deployment spec only sets REDIS_HOST, never DATABASE_URL — so every request to this pod's /items handler crashes and returns 500.
Because kube-proxy round-robins across all 3 endpoints, ~1 in 3 requests (≈33%) hit the broken shop-api pod — matching the alert's reported 31% 5xx rate almost exactly, and explaining the timing (alert fired right as shop-api's readiness probe passed and it joined the endpoint pool, 2m7s into cluster life vs 2m15s for the legitimate pods).

Ruled out
Redis connectivity: healthy api pods log connected to redis at redis:6379 successfully; no redis errors in the error path. Not the cause.
Node/resource press
Add DATABASE_URL to the shop-api Deployment's
